data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note summarizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for Estonia, using a household survey of adults aged 16–65 conducted in 2022–23. Estonia participated for the second time (first participation in 2011–12), enabling comparisons over time and against OECD averages and selected comparison countries. The assessment covers three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—administered exclusively on digital tablets, with proficiency reported on 500-point scales and mapped to discrete proficiency levels. The note reports mean performance and the distribution across levels (e.g., shares at Level 1 or below and at Levels 4–5), plus age, education attainment, gender, and immigrant-background differences. It also describes associations between numeracy proficiency and employment, wages, and well-being/civic engagement, and discusses qualification/skills mismatches. Methodological details on PV and missing-data handling are not provided in the excerpt, and the note is descriptive rather than an ML modeling study.
